as_told.title: Kordylewski cloud as the source of 1920s long-delay radio echoes
as_told.place_text: L5 Lagrangian point between the Earth and the Moon

plain: Radio signals sent in the early 1920s are said to have come back to Earth after a strange delay, and these "long delay echoes" may have bounced off Kordylewski clouds, which are faint clouds of plasma sitting at Lagrangian points, spots in space where the pull of two bodies balances out. Michels takes the idea from the author Robert Temple, who sets it out in his book The New Science of Heaven and in a research paper. Michels does not place the clouds the same way each time: in one episode they lie between the Earth and the Sun, and in another at a balance point between the Earth and the Moon.
